<system-reminder>
Available skills for the Skill tool are listed below. The Skill tool definition relies on this system reminder for valid skill names.

Skills instructions:
When users ask you to perform tasks, check if any available skill can help complete the task more effectively. Skills provide specialized capabilities and domain knowledge.

How to use skills:
- Invoke skills using the Skill tool with the skill name only.
- The skill's prompt will expand and provide detailed instructions on how to complete the task.
- Only use skills listed in the available-skills system reminders or dynamic skill-discovery reminders.
- Do not invoke a skill that is already running.

Available skills:
agent-browser: Automates browsers and Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify, etc.) for testing, form filling, screenshots, and data extraction. Use when the user needs to navigate, interact with, test, or extract data from any website or Electron desktop app.
tuistory: Automates terminal user interface (TUI) testing. Use when you need to launch, interact with, test, or debug terminal applications, capture TUI snapshots, or automate terminal inputs.

ACTIVATE when the user shares a Figma URL (figma.com), mentions Figma designs or components, shares PNG images that may originate from Figma, or when Figma MCP tools are already connected and being used. Handles installation encouragement, conversational promotion, and push-back-to-Figma flows.
install-code-review: Install and configure Factory Droid for automated code review on GitHub or GitLab. Supports single-repo setup or org/group-wide rollout across hundreds of repos. Use when a user wants to set up Droid review on their repositories.
install-triage: Scaffold a scheduled Slack triage automation, generalized to any company. Sets up a Python tool layer (run_triage.py) plus a HEARTBEAT.md agent loop that scans configured Slack channels for actionable messages, dedupes against a ticketing system (Linear or Jira), files tickets, and posts a run summary. Use when the user wants to stand up an automated triage bot.
review: Review code changes and identify high-confidence, actionable bugs. Use when the user wants to: - Review a pull request or branch diff - Find bugs, security issues, or correctness problems in code changes - Get a structured summary of review findings
simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
session-navigation: Navigate, search, and manage Droid sessions. Use when the user wants to: - List recent sessions - Search session history for specific topics or patterns - Resume a previous session - Get details about what was accomplished in a session - Find sessions by project, date, or content

powerpoint: Produce polished PowerPoint presentations (decks, slide shows, pitch decks, any "export to PowerPoint" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint, a slide deck, or a presentation.

install-qa: Set up automated QA testing for this project. Performs deep codebase analysis, asks targeted questions, and generates a modular QA skill with sub-skills per app, a GitHub Actions workflow, and a report template. This is a complex, multi-phase process -- quality assurance is foundational and we take the time to get it right.
security-review: Security-focused code review using STRIDE, OWASP Top 10, OWASP LLM Top 10, and supply chain analysis. Use when: - Reviewing a PR for security vulnerabilities - Performing a security audit of code changes - Identifying injection, auth, data exposure, and other security issues - Running a full-project security audit reviewing every source file
deep-security-review: Correctness-first, depth-first security audit of a single repository. Invoked by /security-review when the user opts into "thorough" mode. Uses a heterogeneous multi-model jury (latest Opus + latest GPT + latest Gemini). A mandatory 3-pass floor (line-anchor verification, vendor prior-art, deep prior-art) runs against every Pass 0 lieutenant-seeded candidate; a conditional escalation tier (dataflow + reachability, exploit construction, adversarial red-team disprove) fires on per-finding triggers. Produces FINDINGS.md, JUDGE.md, DASHBOARD.md, severity-sorted master list, and optional PoC + evidence artifacts for that repo. Never uploads or submits anything; all outputs local.
wiki: Generate comprehensive codebase documentation for a repository. Uploads the wiki to view in the Factory app.

===== BOOT.md =====
# Netmaker bare-metal install — ghostbridge.tech (in-container)

## Access

- **Dashboard:** https://dashboard.ghostbridge.tech
- **API:** https://api.ghostbridge.tech
- **Broker:** wss://broker.ghostbridge.tech

## Credentials

See `/etc/netmaker/credentials.txt` for `MASTER_KEY`, MQTT credentials, and paths.

**DNS required:** `*.ghostbridge.tech` → this container's public IP

---

## Systemd boot order

```
mosquitto → netmaker → caddy → netmaker-first-boot → netclient
```

| Unit | Role |
|------|------|
| `mosquitto.service` | MQTT broker (local WebSocket) |
| `netmaker.service` | API + control plane |
| `caddy.service` | TLS, UI static files, reverse proxy |
| `netmaker-first-boot.service` | One-shot: create network, join netclient |
| `netclient.service` | Daemon with native `netmaker` WireGuard interface |

All units are enabled under `multi-user.target.wants/`.

---

## After the Incus container starts

```bash
systemctl status mosquitto netmaker caddy netmaker-first-boot netclient
journalctl -u netmaker-first-boot -u netclient --no-pager
wg show netmaker
```

---

## Retry first-boot

If first-boot failed or netclient did not join:

```bash
rm -f /var/lib/netmaker/.first-boot-done
systemctl restart netmaker-first-boot
systemctl start netclient
```

---

## Incus host settings (required for in-container WireGuard)

Run on the **Incus host**, not inside the container:

```bash
incus config set <instance> security.nesting true
incus config set <instance> linux.kernel_modules wireguard
```

Also allow these ports to the container:

- **80/tcp**, **443/tcp** (Caddy)
- **51821–51831/udp** (and TCP if used) for WireGuard/netclient

---

## In-container netclient

- Uses **kernel WireGuard** inside the container (not host socket proxy)
- Service grants `CAP_NET_ADMIN`, `CAP_NET_RAW`, `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`
- Starts only after first-boot completes (`/var/lib/netmaker/.first-boot-done`)

---

## Key paths

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/usr/local/bin/netmaker` | Server binary |
| `/usr/local/bin/nmctl` | CLI |
| `/usr/local/bin/netclient` | Client binary |
| `/etc/netmaker/netmaker.env` | Environment config |
| `/etc/netmaker/Caddyfile` | Caddy config (linked from `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`) |
| `/var/lib/netmaker/ui/` | Dashboard static files (served by Caddy) |
| `/var/lib/netmaker/data/` | SQLite database |
| `/etc/netclient/` | Netclient state |
| `/var/log/netmaker-first-boot.log` | First-boot log |

---

## Logs

```bash
journalctl -u netmaker -u netclient -u caddy -u mosquitto -u netmaker-first-boot
tail -f /var/log/netmaker-first-boot.log
```

---

## Chroot / rootfs note

This install was prepared inside an Incus container rootfs (chroot). Systemd units and symlinks are on disk but **services do not run until the container boots with systemd as PID 1**.

To start manually after boot:

```bash
systemctl start mosquitto netmaker caddy
systemctl start netmaker-first-boot   # one-time setup
systemctl start netclient
```

Or rely on enabled units to start automatically at boot.

#!/bin/bash
### BEGIN INIT INFO
# Provides:          netmaker-stack
# Required-Start:    $network $remote_fs
# Required-Stop:     $network $remote_fs
# Default-Start:     2 3 4 5
# Default-Stop:      0 1 6
# Short-Description: Netmaker server stack (mosquitto, netmaker, caddy, netclient)
### END INIT INFO

export PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
ENV=/etc/netmaker/netmaker.env
PIDDIR=/run/netmaker-stack
LOGDIR=/var/log/netmaker-stack
mkdir -p "$PIDDIR" "$LOGDIR"

. /lib/lsb/init-functions 2>/dev/null || true

start_mosquitto() {
  if pgrep -x mosquitto >/dev/null && ss -ltn | grep -q ':1883'; then
    return 0
  fi
  pkill -x mosquitto 2>/dev/null || true
  sleep 1
  if [ -f "$ENV" ]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    source "$ENV"
    mosquitto_passwd -b /etc/mosquitto/netmaker.password "${MQ_USERNAME:-netmaker}" "${MQ_PASSWORD:?}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    chown mosquitto:mosquitto /etc/mosquitto/netmaker.password 2>/dev/null || true
    chmod 600 /etc/mosquitto/netmaker.password
  fi
  start-stop-daemon --start --background --pidfile "$PIDDIR/mosquitto.pid" \
    --make-pidfile --exec /usr/sbin/mosquitto -- -c /etc/mosquitto/mosquitto.conf
}

start_netmaker() {
  if [ -f "$PIDDIR/netmaker.pid" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$PIDDIR/netmaker.pid")" 2>/dev/null; then
    return 0
  fi
  [ -f "$ENV" ] && set -a && source "$ENV" && set +a
  start-stop-daemon --start --background --pidfile "$PIDDIR/netmaker.pid" \
    --make-pidfile --chdir /var/lib/netmaker --exec /usr/local/bin/netmaker \
    >>"$LOGDIR/netmaker.log" 2>&1
}

start_caddy() {
  if [ -f "$PIDDIR/caddy.pid" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$PIDDIR/caddy.pid")" 2>/dev/null; then
    return 0
  fi
  [ -f "$ENV" ] && set -a && source "$ENV" && set +a
  start-stop-daemon --start --background --pidfile "$PIDDIR/caddy.pid" \
    --make-pidfile --exec /usr/bin/caddy -- run --environ --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile \
    >>"$LOGDIR/caddy.log" 2>&1
}

run_first_boot() {
  if [ ! -f /var/lib/netmaker/.first-boot-done ]; then
    /etc/netmaker/first-boot.sh
    touch /var/lib/netmaker/.first-boot-done
  fi
}

start_netclient() {
  if [ -f "$PIDDIR/netclient.pid" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$PIDDIR/netclient.pid")" 2>/dev/null; then
    return 0
  fi
  [ -f /var/lib/netmaker/.first-boot-done ] || return 0
  start-stop-daemon --start --background --pidfile "$PIDDIR/netclient.pid" \
    --make-pidfile --exec /usr/local/bin/netclient -- daemon \
    >>"$LOGDIR/netclient.log" 2>&1
}

wait_api() {
  [ -f "$ENV" ] && set -a && source "$ENV" && set +a
  local i api="http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT:-8081}"
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do
    curl -sf "$api/api/server/health" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MASTER_KEY}" >/dev/null && return 0
    sleep 2
  done
  return 1
}

do_start() {
  log_daemon_msg "Starting Netmaker stack"
  start_mosquitto
  sleep 2
  start_netmaker
  wait_api || log_warning_msg "netmaker API slow to start"
  start_caddy
  run_first_boot
  start_netclient
  log_end_msg 0
}

do_stop() {
  log_daemon_msg "Stopping Netmaker stack"
  for svc in netclient caddy netmaker mosquitto; do
    start-stop-daemon --stop --retry TERM/5/KILL/5 --pidfile "$PIDDIR/${svc}.pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  pkill -f '/usr/local/bin/netmaker' 2>/dev/null || true
  pkill -f 'netclient daemon' 2>/dev/null || true
  log_end_msg 0
}

do_status() {
  for svc in mosquitto netmaker caddy netclient; do
    if [ -f "$PIDDIR/${svc}.pid" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$PIDDIR/${svc}.pid")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "$svc: running (pid $(cat "$PIDDIR/${svc}.pid"))"
    else
      echo "$svc: stopped"
    fi
  done
}

case "${1:-}" in
  start)   do_start ;;
  stop)    do_stop ;;
  restart) do_stop; sleep 2; do_start ;;
  status)  do_status ;;
  *) echo "Usage: $0 {start|stop|restart|status}"; exit 1 ;;
esac
